## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anumānapañha* ("Problems of Inference") constitutes section Mil 6.4.1 of the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. As characterized by Oskar von Hinüber, it is a freestanding, unsubdivided section situated between parts of the work, wherein King Milinda and the elder Nāgasena meet again to discuss the Buddha as a single focal topic [von Hinüber 1996]. The dialogue exhibits stylistic differences from surrounding sections: Milinda addresses the monk with *bhante Nāgasena*, regularly concurs with Nāgasena's explanations, and canonical texts are quoted to support the reasoning [von Hinüber 1996]. Scholars have noted that the conceptual significance of *anumāna* ("inference") here reflects a distinct evolution in philosophical meaning compared to its earlier canonical usage in texts such as the Majjhima Nikāya's *Anumānasutta* [Watanabe 1983].

Curated cross-references on SuttaCentral connect the text to discourses and verses on fragrance and morality, such as Dhammapada vv. 54–56, the *Gandhajātasutta* (AN 3.79), AN 1.616, and the *Satipaṭṭhānakathā* of the Kathāvatthu (Kv 1.9), as well as parallels in the Gāndhārī Dharmapada, Patna Dharmapada, Udānavarga (*Śīlavarga*), and Chinese translations (such as T 210, T 212, and T 213) [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus text-reuse analysis, the section shares 1,489 passages with 130 Pali texts, with the largest volume of matches occurring in the *Milindaṭīkā* (*Sihaḷa-gantha-saṅgaho*), various divisions of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 3, AN 4, AN 5, AN 7, AN 10), the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), and the *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* (Vb 15) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus likewise align passages of the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the Udānavarga, the Patna Dharmapada, the Chinese *Foshuo jiede xiang jing* (T 116), and Mātṛceṭa's *Anaparāddhastotra*, largely agreeing with SuttaCentral's verse parallels [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
